scope: BREAKTHROUGH: bit 1307 is the entity gate; setting it to 1 makes the count store at 0x671698 execute for the first time

the_gate_identified.0x671678: call 0x447190 -> gate bit 1; if 0 -> jumps to 0x6716F0 (the branch measured last round)
the_gate_identified.0x671685: call 0x447190 -> gate bit 2; if 0 -> jumps to 0x6716ED
the_gate_identified.bit_1_equals: body bit 1307 (the bit position measured at 0x671650 entry)

the_previous_measurement_that_proved_it: with snapshot-ent1.bin the probe recorded EntGateA (0x6716F0) exactly once and EntStore never
0x6716F0 is the target of the FIRST gate's zero branch, so gate bit 1 was 0
and reading the files confirmed bit 1307 = 0 in single22, ent1 and the hybrid body alike
which is why the entity list has been empty in every body this project ever produced

the_fix_and_its_result.body: runs/snapshot-ent2.bin = single22 with byte 163 |= 0x08 (bit 1307 = 1) and byte 164 = 0x01 (count = 1)

the_fix_and_its_result.client_after: process gone at the end of the run, so the subsequent per-entity path still needs work

why_this_matters: for the first time the entity count write is reached, which means the entity list is no longer structurally unreachable
the gate was a single bit that every body had wrong, and no amount of field-level work could have fixed it
the client exiting afterwards is the next problem, and it is a DIFFERENT problem: it is about what follows the count (12-bit id, then the per-entity payload)
